rationale: The parent question's remaining scope gap is that every measured case used three voters, where the starved follower is one of three. The harness now takes the voter count as a parameter and the trimmed case is repeated with five voters, so the follower is one of five and the leader keeps a majority of healthy followers while it retries. A local construction run reproduces the same signature (premise: cached claim at index 102 in term 2 over an installed snapshot at 83 in term 3; restores 4 -> 1448 in three seconds with the follower's applied index fixed at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95; the claim persists with the store suffix 84-102 kept; one stable leader set), but that is construction feedback only, so the retained receipt is requested here. The parent question's account is otherwise unchanged and is not re-stated in this update.

scope.description: The trimmed case of the established scenario, run with five voters instead of three: one leader is isolated and appends sixty entries that reach no quorum, is shut down, the remaining four voters elect a leader and commit twenty further entries plus the forced snapshot with TrailingLogs=10, the isolated voter is restarted on its unchanged in-memory log store and reconnected, and its restores, applied and commit indexes, cached claim, store range and the cluster frontier are sampled every 250 ms for three seconds while one entry per sample is applied on the leader.
assumptions: Fault model unchanged: no message loss inside the injected transport; the induced event is one partition of a single voter, its clean shutdown and restart on the same stores.

Only the voter count differs from the established three-voter case; store type, TrailingLogs, write pattern, window and sampling are identical, so a change in the signature would be attributable to the cluster size.
Reused facilities: MakeClusterCustom with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport and MockFSM.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds test code.
Automatic snapshotting stays disabled so the leader's snapshot index is controlled by the explicit Snapshot() call.

experiment.prefix: Same driver as the established trimmed case with the voter count parameter set to five: build the cluster with MakeClusterCustom (counting FSM), commit sixty entries, partition the initial leader, fire sixty applies on it so they are appended without a quorum, wait for it to step down, shut it down with Shutdown().Error(), wait for one of the four remaining voters to be the only stable leader, commit twenty further entries there and force Snapshot(), restart the isolated voter with NewRaft on its original stores and a fresh InmemTransport, reconnect it, emit ca_setup with the tag, the premise fields and the cached claim, wait until its applied index reaches the snapshot index, then sample every 250 ms for three seconds while applying one entry per sample on the leader, emit ca_probe, and disconnect the victim before bounded teardown.
experiment.requirement: A follower that reinstalls the leader's snapshot must remain able to accept subsequent log entries from that leader, or its cached log state must not claim entries the snapshot superseded, independent of how many voters the cluster has.

comparisons.description: Five voters: the follower's FSM was restored again after the first install, i.e. the same snapshot index was re-shipped during the window with the leader's snapshot index unchanged.
Five voters progress predicate: after the window the follower's applied index is still below the cluster frontier although new entries committed and applied elsewhere.
Five voters: the follower's cached last log index is still at or beyond the installed snapshot index with a lower term, and its store still holds that suffix.

experiment.revision_reason: Every measured case of this question used three voters, so the driver now takes the voter count as a parameter and the trimmed case is repeated with five voters, where the starved follower is one of five and the leader retains a majority of healthy followers. Scenario, stores, TrailingLogs, write pattern, window, anchors and the three assertions are otherwise identical to the decided trimmed case; the other cases remain in the file for reuse.
semantic_changes: The scenario driver's voter count became a parameter; the selected case runs the trimmed history with five voters instead of three.
